claims.quote: También se cuenta que los Galipotes, hombres, la mayoría de ellos, se convierten en animales y objetos inanimados que cuidan sus propiedades.

claims.statement: It is believed that people who turn into animals have made pacts with the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, orang yang berubah menjadi hewan telah membuat perjanjian dengan Iblis.
claims.quote: Según se cree, las personas que se vuelven animales han hecho pactos con el Diablo.

claims.statement: The Galipote, also called Zángano or Lugarú, is a legendary creature from the Dominican Republic.
claims.statement_id: Galipote, juga disebut Zángano atau Lugarú, adalah makhluk legendaris dari Republik Dominika.
claims.quote: The Galipote (Spanish pronunciation: [galiˈpote]), also called Zángano (pronounced [ˈsaŋɡano]) or Lugarú (pronounced [luɣaˈɾu]), is a legendary creature from the Dominican Republic

claims.statement: It is characterized by the capacity to transform into various animals and inanimate objects.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini bercirikan kemampuan untuk berubah wujud menjadi bermacam binatang dan benda mati.
claims.quote: It was a mythical being characterized by the ability to transform into different animals and inanimate objects

claims.statement: Legend tells of cruel beings delighting in misleading nocturnal walkers and terrifying the unwary.
claims.statement_id: Dikisahkan sebagai makhluk kejam yang gemar menyesatkan pejalan malam dan menakuti orang.
claims.quote: According to legend, they were cruel and violent beings who enjoyed leading night walkers astray and frightening the unwary.

claims.statement: Originally from San Juan, it probably dates back to the 17th and 18th centuries.
claims.statement_id: Berasal dari San Juan, asal-usulnya mungkin berasal dari antara abad ke-17 dan ke-18.
claims.quote: originally from San Juan, which probably dates back to the 17th and 18th centuries.

claims.statement: It was said to feed on the blood of innocent children, sucked at night, with which it obtained eternal life.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia biasa makan darah anak-anak tak berdosa yang dihisapnya pada malam hari, dan dengannya memperoleh hidup abadi.
claims.quote: It was said that he used to feed on the blood of innocent children (which he sucked during the nights), with which he obtained eternal life

claims.statement: The origin of its power is not entirely clear, but most agree it came from a pact with the devil.
claims.statement_id: Asal kekuatannya tidak sepenuhnya jelas, tetapi kebanyakan sepakat bahwa itu berasal dari perjanjian dengan setan.
claims.quote: The origin of his power is not entirely clear, however, most agree that it was due to a pact with the devil

claims.statement: There is a belief in a galipote able to turn only into a dog, called lugaru, a term that seems to come from French loup-garou, the legendary werewolf.
claims.statement_id: Ada kepercayaan tentang galipote yang hanya dapat berubah menjadi anjing, disebut lugaru, istilah yang tampaknya berasal dari bahasa Prancis loup-garou untuk manusia serigala.
claims.quote: There is a belief in a galipote capable of turning exclusively into a dog, known as lugaru (a term that seems to come from the French loup-garou, a name used for the legendary werewolf or lycanthrope).

claims.statement: Another subspecies (rendered "drone" in this source, or zancú) is also mentioned, able to take strides as long as the distance between one river and the next and even to become invisible.
claims.statement_id: Disebut pula subspesies lain (dalam sumber ini disebut "drone", atau zancú) yang mampu melangkah sejauh jarak antara satu sungai dan sungai lain, bahkan bisa menjadi tak terlihat.
claims.quote: There is also talk of another subspecies known as drone or zancú, characterized by the ability to walk with strides (as long as the distance between one river and another), capable even of becoming invisible.

claims.statement: According to popular belief, the galipote was vulnerable only to a stake from a tree known as palo de cruz, which had to be cut specifically on Good Friday.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan populer, galipote hanya rentan terhadap pasak dari pohon yang disebut palo de cruz, yang harus ditebang khusus pada Jumat Agung.
claims.quote: According to popular belief, the galipote was only vulnerable to a stake from a tree known as palo de cruz, which had to be cut specifically on Good Friday.

claims.statement: The legend is so deeply rooted that in some areas walkers do not go out at night without protective amulets or reciting a spell.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini begitu mengakar sehingga di beberapa daerah para pejalan tidak keluar malam tanpa jimat pelindung atau membaca mantra.
claims.quote: The legend is so deep-rooted that, in some areas of the country, walkers do not go out at night without protective amulets or reciting some spell.

claims.statement: It also enjoys atrocious strength and immunity against firearms.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga memiliki kekuatan dahsyat dan kebal terhadap senjata api.
claims.quote: as well as enjoying atrocious strength and immunity against firearms.

claims.statement: The Diccionario del español dominicano, as cited in this column, defines the galipote as a "person who, according to popular belief, has the ability to turn into an animal or a tree".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Diccionario del español dominicano yang dikutip kolom ini, galipote adalah "orang yang menurut kepercayaan populer berkemampuan berubah menjadi hewan atau pohon".
claims.quote: El galipote es una “Persona que, según la creencia popular, tiene la facultad de convertirse en animal o en árbol.

claims.statement: According to this column, the word entered Dominican Spanish through Haitian Creole galipòt, galpòt, gayipòt, a mythical animal resembling the lugarú (lougawou).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kolom ini, kata itu masuk ke bahasa Spanyol Dominika lewat Kreol Haiti galipòt, galpòt, gayipòt, hewan mitos yang menyerupai lugarú (lougawou).
claims.quote: La voz del título entró al español dominicano a través del criollo haitiano, galipòt, galpòt, gayipòt, que es un animal mítico que se asemeja al lugarú (lougawou).

claims.statement: The column says the French galipote closest to the Dominican one was known in the Centre-West and Auvergne of France, where the word named a monstrous animal wandering the fields at night.
claims.statement_id: Kolom ini menyebut galipote Prancis yang paling dekat dikenal di wilayah Centre-Ouest dan Auvergne, tempat kata itu menamai hewan monster yang berkeliaran malam hari di ladang.
claims.quote: El galipote francés más próximo del dominicano es el que se conoció en la región del Centro-Oeste y Auvernia en Francia, en la que se empleaba la voz para designar un animal monstruoso que deambulaba por la noche en los campos.

claims.statement: From there the word passed into Dominican Spanish to name a person who makes an evil pact and can turn into an animal or a tree.
claims.statement_id: Dari sana kata itu masuk ke bahasa Spanyol Dominika untuk menyebut orang yang membuat perjanjian jahat dan dapat berubah menjadi hewan atau pohon.
claims.quote: De aquí pasó al español dominicano para denominar a una persona que hace un pacto maléfico y puede convertirse en animal o árbol.

claims.statement: The column quotes a Dominican folklorist: among the most widespread rural beliefs is that some people can turn into animals and inanimate objects; those credited with this power are called "Galipotes o Dundunes".
claims.statement_id: Kolom ini mengutip folkloris Dominika: salah satu kepercayaan paling meluas di pedesaan adalah bahwa sebagian orang dapat berubah menjadi hewan dan benda mati; mereka yang dianggap berkuasa itu disebut "Galipotes o Dundunes".
claims.quote: Entre las creencias más extendidas en las zonas rurales dominicanas está la de atribuir a algunas personas la facultad de convertirse en animales y en objetos inanimados; los individuos a quienes se atribuye ese poder sobrenatural son llamados “Galipotes o Dundunes”.

claims.statement: The stories are heard in all regions of the country, more often in the South and near the Haitian border; few present Galipotes as interested in causing physical harm.
claims.statement_id: Cerita-cerita itu terdengar di seluruh negeri, lebih sering di Selatan dan dekat perbatasan Haiti; hanya sedikit yang menampilkan Galipote ingin mencelakai secara fisik.
claims.quote: Tales historias, que se escuchan en todas las regiones del país, son más frecuentes en el Sur y en las poblaciones cercanas a la frontera con Haití. Son pocas las historias en las que se presentan a los Galipotes como seres interesados en provocar daños físicos.

claims.statement: More numerous are stories in which they play mischievous tricks, such as blocking night walkers and confusing their way.
claims.statement_id: Lebih banyak cerita yang menampilkan Galipote berbuat jahil, seperti menghalangi pejalan malam dan mengacaukan jalan mereka.
claims.quote: Abundan más aquellas en las que aparecen haciendo bellaquerías, como impedir el paso a los caminantes nocturnos y confundirles los caminos.

claims.statement: It is also told that Galipotes, mostly men, turn into animals and inanimate objects that guard their property.
claims.statement_id: Diceritakan pula bahwa para Galipote, kebanyakan laki-laki, berubah menjadi hewan dan benda mati yang menjaga harta milik mereka.
claims.quote: También se cuenta que los Galipotes, hombres, la mayoría de ellos, se convierten en animales y objetos inanimados que cuidan sus propiedades.

claims.statement: It is believed that people who turn into animals have made pacts with the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, orang yang berubah menjadi hewan telah membuat perjanjian dengan Iblis.
claims.quote: Según se cree, las personas que se vuelven animales han hecho pactos con el Diablo.

claims.statement: The Gougou is one of the oldest Mi'kmaq legends in Canadian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Gougou adalah salah satu legenda Mi'kmaq tertua dalam cerita rakyat Kanada.
claims.quote: The Gougou is one of the oldest Mi'kmaq legends in Canadian folklore.

claims.statement: Described as an ogress residing on Miscou Island in northeastern New Brunswick.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan sebagai raksasa wanita pemakan manusia yang tinggal di Pulau Miscou, New Brunswick.
claims.quote: It is said to be ogress that lives on Miscou Island, located in northeast New Brunswick in the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

claims.statement: Mentioned by explorer Samuel de Champlain during his regional exploration in 1603.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini disebutkan oleh Samuel de Champlain dalam catatan penjelajahannya tahun 1603.
claims.quote: It was mentioned by Samuel de Champlain when writing about his exploration of the area in 1603.

claims.statement: Champlain records that near the Bay of Chaleurs, towards the south, there is an island where a terrible monster lives that his informants (called "savages" in the text) name Gougou and described as having the form of a woman, though very frightful.
claims.statement_id: Champlain mencatat bahwa dekat Teluk Chaleurs, ke arah selatan, ada sebuah pulau tempat tinggal monster mengerikan yang disebut Gougou oleh para penutur (disebut "savages" dalam teks) dan digambarkan berbentuk perempuan yang sangat menakutkan.
claims.quote: near the Bay of Chaleurs, towards the south, there is an island where a terrible monster resides, which the savages call Gougou, and which they told me had the form of a woman, though very frightful

claims.statement: Its size is described as so great that the tops of the masts of Champlain's vessel would not reach to its middle.
claims.statement_id: Ukurannya digambarkan begitu besar sehingga puncak tiang kapal Champlain tidak akan mencapai pinggangnya.
claims.quote: of such a size that they told me the tops of the masts of our vessel would not reach to his middle, so great do they picture him

claims.statement: They say it has often devoured and still devours many people; when it can catch them it puts them into a great pocket and then eats them.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan ia sering memangsa dan masih terus memangsa banyak orang; bila dapat menangkap mereka, ia memasukkannya ke kantong besar lalu memakannya.
claims.quote: they say that he has often devoured and still continues to devour many savages; these he puts, when he can catch them, into a great pocket, and afterwards eats them

claims.statement: Those who escaped the creature's jaws said its pocket was so great it could have held Champlain's vessel; the monster makes horrible noises on the island.
claims.statement_id: Mereka yang lolos dari rahang makhluk malang itu mengatakan kantongnya begitu besar hingga dapat memuat kapal Champlain; monster ini membuat bunyi mengerikan di pulau itu.
claims.quote: those who had escaped the jaws of this wretched creature said that its pocket was so great that it could have put our vessel into it. This monster makes horrible noises in this island

claims.statement: Prevert of St. Malo told Champlain that, while searching for mines, he passed so near the creature's dwelling that he and everyone aboard heard strange hissings from its noise.
claims.statement_id: Prevert dari St. Malo menuturkan bahwa saat mencari tambang ia melewati begitu dekat tempat tinggal makhluk itu sehingga ia dan seluruh awak kapalnya mendengar desisan aneh dari suaranya.
claims.quote: Even the above-mentioned Prevert from St. Malo told me that, while going in search of mines, as mentioned in the previous chapter, he passed so near the dwelling-place of this frightful creature, that he and all those on board his vessel heard strange hissings from the noise it made

claims.statement: Champlain writes that all the Indigenous people fear it and tell such strange things that it would be regarded as a myth, but he holds that the place is the dwelling of some devil that torments them.
claims.statement_id: Champlain menulis bahwa semua penduduk asli takut kepadanya dan menceritakan hal-hal yang begitu aneh hingga dianggap mitos, tetapi ia berpendapat tempat itu adalah kediaman semacam iblis yang menyiksa mereka.
claims.quote: What makes me believe what they say is the fact that all the savages in general fear it, and tell such strange things about it that, if I were to record all they say, it would be regarded as a myth; but I hold that this is the dwelling-place of some devil that torments them in the above-mentioned manner.

claims.statement: French Wikipedia calls the Gougou one of the oldest legends of Mi'kmaq origin, about an ogress living on the Miscou plain near the Bay of Chaleurs, south of the Gaspé and on the edge of Acadia, in North America.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia Prancis menyebut Gougou sebagai salah satu legenda tertua asal Mi'kmaq, tentang ogresse yang tinggal di dataran Miscou dekat Teluk Chaleurs, di selatan Gaspésie dan perbatasan Acadie, Amerika Utara.
claims.quote: La Gougou (la Roulotte) est l'une des plus vieilles légendes d'origine micmaque racontant la légende d'une ogresse vivant dans la plaine de Miscou près de la baie des Chaleurs, au sud de la Gaspésie et aux confins de l'Acadie, en Amérique du Nord.

claims.statement: William F. Ganong made attempts to uncover the legend when surveying the area in 1903.
claims.statement_id: William F. Ganong berusaha menggali legenda ini saat menyurvei daerah itu pada 1903.
claims.quote: William F. Ganong made attempts to uncover the legend when surveying the area in 1903.

claims.statement: Gualichu, or gualicho, was an evil spirit or demon in Mapuche and Tehuelche cultures.
claims.statement_id: Gualichu atau gualicho dalam mitologi Mapuche dan Tehuelche adalah roh jahat atau iblis.
claims.quote: Gualichu, or gualicho, in Mapuche mythology and mainly in the Tehuelche culture, was an evil spirit or demon, comparable but not similar to the Devil.

claims.statement: Gualichu was not worshipped but feared, held responsible for every disease or calamity.
claims.statement_id: Gualichu tidak disembah melainkan ditakuti dan dipersalahkan atas segala penyakit serta musibah.
claims.quote: As the Araucanians had not a properly called god of evil, Gualichu was not worshipped but feared. He was blamed for every disease or calamity

claims.statement: He could enter bodies or objects, requiring an exorcism to expel him.
claims.statement_id: Gualichu dapat merasuki tubuh manusia atau benda sehingga diperlukan eksorsisme untuk mengusirnya.
claims.quote: Gualichu could enter people's body or objects and then an exorcism had to be performed to expel him

claims.statement: By extension the term is used for an evil spell, charm or jinx ("It has Gualichu"); in that sense the word became gualicho and survives in the folklore of Chile, Argentina, southern Brazil and Uruguay as a noun and a verb (engualichar, to cast an evil spell on someone or something).
claims.statement_id: Secara perluasan, istilah ini dipakai untuk guna-guna atau kutukan ("It has Gualichu"); dalam arti itu kata tersebut menjadi gualicho dan masih hidup dalam cerita rakyat Chile, Argentina, selatan Brasil, dan Uruguay sebagai kata benda dan kata kerja (engualichar, menyihir seseorang atau sesuatu).
claims.quote: By extension, the term applied to an evil spell or charm, or a jinx ("It has Gualichu"). In this sense the word has evolved into gualicho and still survives in the local folklore of Chile, Argentina, south of Brazil and Uruguay, in the form of a noun and a verb (engualichar, to cast an evil spell on somebody or something).

claims.statement: He was a purely spiritual being with no depiction, and was believed to live underground.
claims.statement_id: Ia makhluk yang murni rohani dan tidak ada penggambarannya; ia dipercaya tinggal di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: He was a purely spiritual being and there is no depiction of him. He was believed to live underground.

claims.statement: According to the museum, the Tehuelche believed in evil beings, the Gualichu, who dwelt in the underworld and were always looking for ways to do harm.
claims.statement_id: Menurut museum itu, orang Tehuelche percaya akan adanya makhluk-makhluk jahat, para Gualichu, yang berdiam di dunia bawah dan selalu mencari cara untuk mencelakai.
claims.quote: The Tehuelche believed in the existence of evil beings, the Gualichu, who dwelt in the underworld and were always looking for ways to do harm.

claims.statement: Some stories suggest the Gualichu was actually a single evil being, although this understanding may come from Mapuche influence in the northern reaches of Tehuelche territory.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian cerita menyiratkan bahwa Gualichu sebenarnya satu makhluk jahat, meskipun pemahaman itu mungkin berasal dari pengaruh Mapuche di wilayah utara Tehuelche.
claims.quote: Some stories suggest that the Gualichu was actually a single evil being, although this understanding may have come from the Mapuche influence in the northern reaches of Tehuelche territory.

claims.statement: The Headless Nun is a ghost legend tied to French Fort Cove in Miramichi, New Brunswick.
claims.statement_id: Headless Nun adalah kisah hantu yang dikaitkan dengan French Fort Cove di Miramichi, New Brunswick.
claims.quote: The Headless Nun is a ghost story associated with French Fort Cove in Nordin, now the City of Miramichi, New Brunswick.

claims.statement: The figure was an 18th-century inhabitant named Sister Marie Inconnue.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh biarawati tanpa kepala ini adalah penduduk abad ke-18 bernama Sister Marie Inconnue.
claims.quote: the Headless Nun was an 18th-century resident of the area named Sister Marie Inconnue

claims.statement: In one version, a mad trapper severed her head and escaped into the woods.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi, seorang penjerat gila memenggal kepalanya dan membawanya lari ke hutan.
claims.quote: in one version, a "mad trapper" cut off her head and ran into the woods with it.

claims.statement: In another version, two sailors cut off her head after she refused to divulge the location of a treasure.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain, dua pelaut memenggal kepalanya setelah ia menolak membocorkan lokasi harta karun.
claims.quote: In another, two sailors cut off her head after she refused to divulge the location of a treasure.

claims.statement: The story holds that Sister Marie's head was never found, so her spirit forever roams the area searching for it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, kepala Suster Marie tidak pernah ditemukan, sehingga rohnya terus berkeliaran di daerah itu untuk mencarinya.
claims.quote: The story holds that Sister Marie's head was never found, resulting in her spirit forever roaming the area in search of it.

claims.statement: In the tour guide's telling, one night around 1758, after helping a woman through a difficult childbirth, Sister Marie Inconnue was returning to the settlement at the cove, then home to a battery of 16 cannons and a small detachment of soldiers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penuturan pemandu wisata, sekitar 1758, setelah menolong seorang perempuan melahirkan dengan sulit, Suster Marie Inconnue pulang ke permukiman di teluk kecil itu, yang saat itu memiliki baterai 16 meriam dan sepasukan kecil tentara.
claims.quote: one night, around 1758, after having helped a woman through a difficult childbirth, Sister Marie Inconnue was returning to the settlement at the cove — at the time home to a battery of 16 cannons and a small detachment of soldiers.

claims.statement_id: Ketika ia menyeberangi jembatan kecil di atas Crow Brook, ia diserang. Ada yang mengatakan pelakunya dua pelaut berkusta dari L'Indienne de Morlaix yang membalas dendam; yang lain berkeras pelakunya seorang penjerat liar yang putus asa setelah bertahun-tahun hidup di hutan.

claims.statement_id: Headless Nun Tour adalah tur berpemandu satu jam di French Fort Cove yang berlangsung setelah gelap, dengan pemandu berkostum menuturkan kisah biarawati tanpa kepala yang dianggap menghantui teluk itu.

claims.statement: Huenchula is a character belonging to the mythology of the Chiloé archipelago in Chile.
claims.statement_id: Huenchula adalah tokoh mitologi dari kepulauan Chiloé di Chile.
claims.quote: es un personaje perteneciente a la mitología del archipiélago de Chiloé (Chile).

claims.statement: Huenchula was a maiden from Cucao on the western coast who loved an aquatic being.
claims.statement_id: Huenchula adalah gadis dari Cucao di Isla Grande de Chiloé yang menjalin asmara dengan makhluk air.
claims.quote: Se cuenta que la Huenchula es una muchacha de la zona de Cucao (costa occidental de la Isla Grande de Chiloé) que tenía amores con un ser acuático

claims.statement: She was taken by him and transformed into a guardian of the ocean's fertility.
claims.statement_id: Ia dibawa oleh makhluk air dan diubah menjadi penjaga kesuburan samudra.
claims.quote: fue secuestrada por él y convertida luego en guardiana de la fecundidad del océano.

claims.statement: There are several versions of the story that differ in many elements, such as the girl's relationship with her parents, with the fantastic being who took her, or the fate of their baby, but all place the events in the Lake Cucao area.
claims.statement_id: Ada beberapa versi cerita yang berbeda dalam banyak unsur, misalnya hubungan gadis itu dengan orang tuanya, hubungannya dengan makhluk gaib yang membawanya, atau nasib bayi mereka, tetapi semuanya menempatkan peristiwa di sekitar danau Cucao.
claims.quote: Existen varias versiones de la historia, que difieren en numerosos elementos, tales como la relación que existía entre la muchacha y sus padres, entre ella y el ser fantástico que se la llevó o el destino del bebé que tuvieron, pero todas sitúan los hechos en la zona del lago Cucao

claims.statement: A Huilliche myth about the origin of Lake Cucao recorded in the 18th century is seen as the first version of the tale.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Huilliche tentang asal danau Cucao yang dicatat pada abad ke-18 dipandang sebagai versi pertama cerita ini.
claims.quote: Un mito huilliche acerca del origen del lago Cucao que fue registrado en el siglo XVIII, es visto como la primera versión de relato.

claims.statement: According to the legend, the Huenchula was a Huilliche girl born of a machi named Huenchur and a woodcutter.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Huenchula adalah gadis Huilliche, anak seorang machi bernama Huenchur dan seorang penebang kayu.
claims.quote: De acuerdo a la leyenda, la Huenchula era una joven huilliche nacida de la unión de una machi, llamada Huenchur, y de un leñador.

claims.statement: Her mother had warned her not to look at herself in the well, since she might not see her reflection but the Millalobo taking on her appearance to watch her unnoticed.
claims.statement_id: Ibunya telah memperingatkannya agar tidak bercermin di sumur, sebab yang terlihat mungkin bukan bayangannya, melainkan Millalobo yang menyerupainya untuk mengamatinya tanpa ketahuan.
claims.quote: Su madre le había advertido que no debía mirarse en el pozo, pues podía ser que no viera su reflejo, sino que el Millalobo tomara su aspecto para observarla sin ser notado.

claims.statement: After a year the Huenchula came to her mother's house with a bundle in her arms and greeted her naturally, as if she had never left, saying she had married a fish.
claims.statement_id: Setahun kemudian Huenchula datang ke rumah ibunya sambil menggendong bungkusan, menyapanya seolah tak pernah berpisah, dan berkata bahwa ia telah menikah dengan seekor ikan.
claims.quote: Al cabo de un año, la Huenchula llegó a la casa de su madre con un bulto en sus brazos y la saludó con naturalidad como si nunca se hubiera separado de ella y diciéndole que se había casado con un pez.

claims.statement: Her husband, the being known as Millalobo, told her to stop crying because her daughter was not dead, and then a beautiful young woman named Pincoya emerged, the daughter of them both.
claims.statement_id: Suaminya, makhluk yang dikenal sebagai Millalobo, menyuruhnya berhenti menangis karena putrinya belum mati; lalu muncul seorang gadis cantik bernama Pincoya, putri mereka berdua.
claims.quote: Su esposo, el ser conocido como Millalobo le dijo que dejara de llorar ya que su hija no estaba muerta, y luego de decir esto, emergió una bella joven llamada Pincoya; la cual era la hija de ambos.

claims.statement: They all went to live in the palace the Millalobo has at the bottom of the sea; over the years the Huenchula and the Millalobo had two more children, called Pincoy and Sirena.
claims.statement_id: Mereka semua pergi tinggal di istana Millalobo di dasar laut; bertahun-tahun kemudian Huenchula dan Millalobo mendapat dua anak lagi bernama Pincoy dan Sirena.
claims.quote: así todos se fueron a vivir al palacio que el Millalobo tiene en el fondo del mar. Al pasar los años, la Huenchula y el Millalobo tendrían dos hijos más; llamados Pincoy y Sirena.

claims.statement: The Millalobo lives at the bottom of the sea with his wife Huenchula and their three children, the Pincoya, the Pincoy and the Sirena Chilota, who help him manage the seas.
claims.statement_id: Millalobo tinggal di dasar laut bersama istrinya Huenchula dan ketiga anak mereka, Pincoya, Pincoy, dan Sirena Chilota, yang membantunya mengelola lautan.

claims.statement: Idlirvirissong is an evil spirit in the religion of the Inuit of Baffin Island and Greenland.

claims.quote: Idlirvirissong, or Irdlirvirisissong, is an evil spirit in the religion of the Inuit of Baffin Island and the Greenlandic Inuit.

claims.statement: Depicted as a clown with an upturned nose, she possesses numerous dogs.
claims.statement_id: Sosok ini digambarkan menyerupai badut dengan hidung melengkung ke atas dan memiliki banyak anjing.
claims.quote: Idlirvirissong is a demonic, evil spirit usually depicted as a clown, with a nose "turned up on the side." She owns many dogs

claims.statement: She is described as the cousin and adversary of the spirit of the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut sebagai sepupu dan penentang dari roh Matahari.
claims.quote: Idlirvirissong is said to be the cousin of the spirit of the Sun, to whom she is opposed

claims.quote: In most descriptions, Idlirvirissong is a female, though some give Idlirvirissong's gender as a male.

claims.statement: Idlirvirissong lives in a house in the sky with her dogs, awaiting the newly deceased; when they arrive she dances, saying "Qimitiaka nexessaqtaqpaka" ("I am looking for food for my dogs").
claims.statement_id: Idlirvirissong tinggal di rumah di langit bersama anjing-anjingnya, menanti kedatangan orang yang baru meninggal; ketika mereka tiba ia menari sambil berkata "Qimitiaka nexessaqtaqpaka" ("Aku mencari makanan untuk anjing-anjingku").
claims.quote: Idlirvirissong lives in a house in the sky with her dogs, where she awaits the arrival of the newly deceased. When the deceased arrive, Idlirvirissong will dance while saying "Qimitiaka nexessaqtaqpaka" ("I am looking for food for my dogs").

claims.statement: Those who laugh at Idlirvirissong and her dance have their bodies cut open and their intestines placed on her plate called qengmerping and fed to the dogs; those who do not laugh are spared.
claims.statement_id: Mereka yang menertawakan Idlirvirissong dan tariannya akan dibelah tubuhnya, ususnya diletakkan di piring bernama qengmerping dan diberikan kepada anjing; yang tidak tertawa dibiarkan selamat.
claims.quote: Those who laugh at Idlirvirissong and her dance will have their bodies cut open, and their intestines placed on a Idlirvirissong's plate called qengmerping and be fed to the dogs. Those who do not laugh are spared.

claims.statement: In other parts of Greenland she is known as the Erdlaveersissok, the "entrail-seizer"; on Baffin Island a similar figure called Ululiernang or Ululiarnåq is present.
claims.statement_id: Di bagian lain Greenland ia dikenal sebagai Erdlaveersissok, "perebut isi perut"; di Pulau Baffin terdapat tokoh serupa bernama Ululiernang atau Ululiarnåq.
claims.quote: In other parts of Greenland, she is known as the Erdlaveersissok, the "entrail-seizer." In Baffin Island a similar figure known as Ululiernang or Ululiarnåq is present.

claims.statement: In some versions she is instead the cousin of the Moon spirit Aningan; in one version told by the Inuit of Smith Sound, Aningan warns people not to laugh around Idlirvirissong.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi ia sepupu roh Bulan, Aningan; dalam satu versi yang dituturkan Inuit Smith Sound, Aningan memperingatkan orang agar tidak tertawa di dekat Idlirvirissong.
claims.quote: in some versions, she is the cousin of the Moon spirit Aningan instead. In one version recounted by the Inuit of Smith Sound, Aningan warns people not to laugh around Idlirvirissong.

claims.statement: Kroeber (1899) records that besides his wife and sister, Aningan has a female cousin, Irdlirvirisissong, who lives in the sky in a separate house, sometimes visits Aningan, and has her nose turned up on the sides.
claims.statement_id: Kroeber (1899) mencatat bahwa selain istri dan saudarinya, Aningan memiliki sepupu perempuan, Irdlirvirisissong, yang tinggal di langit di rumah terpisah, kadang mengunjungi Aningan, dan hidungnya terlipat ke atas di sisi-sisinya.
claims.quote: Irdlirvirisissong. She lives in the sky, but in a separate house, and sometimes visits Aningan. Her nose is turned up on the sides.

claims.statement: Kroeber's record says that those who laugh she cuts open and gives their entrails to the dogs, while others are spared.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan Kroeber, orang yang tertawa dibelahnya dan isi perutnya diberikan kepada anjing, sedangkan yang lain dibiarkan.
claims.quote: Those of the people that laugh, she cuts open, and gives their entrails to the dogs. Others are spared.

claims.statement: In Greenland she is called Erdlaveersissok ("the entrail-seizer"); residing on the way to the moon, she tempts people to laugh by her dancing and grimaces and, if successful, takes out their intestines.
claims.statement_id: Di Greenland ia disebut Erdlaveersissok ("perebut isi perut"); tinggal di jalan menuju bulan, ia menggoda orang tertawa dengan tarian dan seringai, dan bila berhasil mengeluarkan usus mereka.
claims.quote: In Greenland she is called' Erdlaveersissok' ('the entrail-seizer'). Residing on the way to the moon, she tempts people to laugh by her dancing and grimaces, and if successful takes out their intestines.

claims.statement: According to Kroeber, on Baffin Land the story is told as in Greenland, except that the woman, there the wife of the moon, is named Ululiernang.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kroeber, di Pulau Baffin kisahnya sama seperti di Greenland, hanya saja perempuan itu, di sana istri bulan, bernama Ululiernang.
claims.quote: In Baffin Land the story is told as in Greenland, except that the woman, who is here the wife of the moon, is named Ululiernang.

claims.statement: Ululiernang has a hollow back and no entrails, and she offers the entrails she obtains to the moon's ermine.
claims.statement_id: Ululiernang berpunggung berongga dan tanpa isi perut, dan ia mempersembahkan isi perut yang diperolehnya kepada cerpelai milik bulan.
claims.quote: Ululiernang has a hollow back with her entrails missing, and she offers the entrails she acquired to the moon's ermine.

claims.statement: The Iemisch is a cryptid from Patagonia, specifically near the Lake Colhué region.
claims.statement_id: Iemisch adalah makhluk kriptid dari Patagonia, khususnya di pegunungan dekat kawasan Danau Colhué.
claims.quote: The Iemisch (a.k.a. Iemisch Listai) is a supposed cryptid from Patagonia, specifically in the mountains near the Lake Colhué region.

claims.statement: It is nocturnal and powerful enough to seize horses and drag them underwater.
claims.statement_id: Hewan nokturnal ini begitu kuat sehingga mampu mencengkeram kuda lalu menyeretnya ke dasar air.
claims.quote: The animal is of nocturnal habits, and it's said to be so strong that it can seize horses with its claws and drag them to the bottom of the water.

claims.statement: Lehmann-Nitsche writes that the word Jemisch, which according to Ameghino the Patagonian natives use for that Neomylodon, most probably means the otter (Lutra felina).
claims.statement_id: Lehmann-Nitsche menulis bahwa kata Jemisch, yang menurut Ameghino dipakai penduduk asli Patagonia untuk menyebut Neomylodon, kemungkinan besar berarti berang-berang (Lutra felina).
claims.quote: La palabra Jemisch (capítulo 11) con que según el señor Ameghino los indígenas de la Patagonia designan á aquel Neomylodon, significa muy probablemente la lutra (Lutra felina Mol.)

claims.statement: First attested by Florentino Ameghino in 1897; a full study appeared in the 1955 book On the Track of Unknown Animals.
claims.statement_id: Pertama dicatat oleh Florentino Ameghino pada 1897; kajian lengkapnya terbit dalam buku On the Track of Unknown Animals tahun 1955.
claims.quote: First attested to by Florentino Ameghino in 1897, a full study on the creature was published in the 1955 book On the Track of Unknown Animals.

claims.statement: According to the description in the original letter, it has a short head, big canines and no external ears, short plantigrade feet with three toes on the forefeet and four on the hind ones, webbed for swimming and armed with formidable claws, and a long, flat, prehensile tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi dalam surat asli, kepalanya pendek, bertaring besar, tanpa telinga luar, berkaki pendek plantigrad dengan tiga jari depan dan empat belakang berselaput renang dan bercakar kuat, berekor panjang, pipih, dan dapat menggenggam.
claims.quote: According to the description I have been given, it has a short head, big canine teeth, and no external ears: its feet are short and plantigrade, with three toes on the forefeet and four on the hind, three toaes are formed by a membrane for swimming, and are also armed with formidable claws. Its tail is long, flat and prehensile.

claims.statement: It reportedly could move as quickly on land as in water and was described as having a "soul-wrenching scream".
claims.statement_id: Konon ia bergerak secepat di darat seperti di air, dan digambarkan memiliki jeritan "soul-wrenching".
claims.quote: It reportedly could move as quickly on land as in the water, and was described as having a "soul-wrenching scream".

claims.statement: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche, a German anthropologist in Argentina, claimed to have a sample of iemisch skin from a local rancher, with small bone plates embedded in it that protected the creature from arrowheads.
claims.statement_id: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche, antropolog Jerman di Argentina, mengaku memiliki contoh kulit iemisch dari seorang peternak setempat, dengan keping tulang kecil tertanam di kulit yang melindunginya dari mata panah.
claims.quote: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche, a German anthropologist working in Argentina, claimed to have a sample of the iemisch's skin given to him by a local rancher. He stated that there were small bone plates embedded in its skin, which protected the creature from arrowheads.

claims.statement: Lehmann-Nitsche and Santiago Roth later published more iemisch tales, concluding it must be an unknown type of otter; paleontologist John Bell Hatcher noted that despite spending as much time with Patagonian natives he had never heard of such a creature.
claims.statement_id: Lehmann-Nitsche dan Santiago Roth kemudian menerbitkan lebih banyak kisah iemisch dan menyimpulkan bahwa iemisch tentulah sejenis berang-berang yang belum dikenal; paleontolog John Bell Hatcher mencatat bahwa walau lama bersama penduduk asli Patagonia ia tak pernah mendengar makhluk semacam itu.
claims.quote: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche and Santiago Roth would eventually publish more iemisch tales, concluding that the iemisch must be an unknown type of otter. Upon peer review, paleontologist John Bell Hatcher noted that though he had spent equal amounts of time with Patagonian natives, he had never heard of such a creature.

claims.statement: Later scholars also cast doubt on Heuvelmans's research, noting that the word 'Iemisch' is not associated with any language spoken in Patagonia.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana kemudian meragukan penelitian Heuvelmans, mencatat bahwa kata 'Iemisch' tidak dikaitkan dengan bahasa mana pun yang dituturkan di Patagonia.
claims.quote: Later scholars also cast doubt on research by Heuvelmans, noting that the word 'Iemisch' isn't associated with any language spoken in Patagonia.

claims.statement: Lehmann-Nitsche argues that the Indians' myths, legends and tales of a fierce animal mostly may refer to the jaguar (tigre).

claims.quote: Los mitos (capítulo III), leyendas y cuentos de los indios en que se habla de un animal feroz, pueden referirse en su mayoría al tigre

claims.statement: Lehmann-Nitsche lists other spellings of the name from earlier recorders: Chimchimen (de la Cruz and Gay), Jémechim (Lista), Yem'chen (Moreno), Jemisch (Carlos Ameghino) and Hymché (Tournouer).

claims.quote: « Chimchimen », de la Cruz y Gay. «Jémechim», Lista. « Yem'chen», Moreno. «Jemisch», Carlos Ameghino. « Hymché », Tournouer.
